claude.sample_unit: cardiac surgery scenarios (rated by 5 surgeons; 3,750 binary ratings)

links.outcome: Evaluator detection of incorrect LLM outputs; overacceptance vs underrecognition rate between rounds
links.effect: Overacceptance 7.57% vs underrecognition 2.59% (net gap +4.98%, p<0.001); in five highest-weighted dimensions 10.16% vs 3.68% (net +6.48%).
links.quote: The overall overacceptance rate (affirmative-to-negative revisions) was 7.57%, whereas the underrecognition rate (negative-to-affirmative revisions) was 2.59%, yielding a net trust calibration gap of +4.98% (McNemar's test, p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Experts failing to recognize incorrect or hallucinated LLM output on first-pass review
links.effect: Experienced surgeons often missed LLM errors at first glance; 10.16% of ratings in top-weighted dimensions revised affirmative to negative after seeing reference answers.
links.quote: Notably, even experienced experts often failed to recognize LLM errors at first glance

links.outcome: Automation bias from fluent, well-structured LLM outputs suppressing clinician scrutiny
links.effect: Overacceptance concentrated in safety-critical dimensions; overacceptance rate 10.16% nearly three times underrecognition 3.68%, net gap +6.48%.
links.quote: This indicates that expert trust miscalibration was concentrated in precisely the dimensions where errors carry the greatest clinical consequence—a finding consistent with automation bias, whereby plausible and fluently structured outputs reduce the likelihood of critical human scrutiny.

links.outcome: LLM clinical knowledge and reasoning quality in complex cardiac surgery scenarios
links.effect: Median normalized scores 0.896 (O1) to 0.521 (Llama3-OpenBioLLM-70B); patient safety mean score 0.507; scenarios with complex longitudinal reasoning scored lowest (0.458, 0.430).
links.quote: Patient safety (Q2) had the lowest average score (0.507); even the best-performing model, O1, reached only 0.600, while Llama3-OpenBioLLM-70B scored 0.307.

links.outcome: LLM accuracy on quantitative device sizing (mitral annuloplasty ring)
links.effect: Four of five models recommended 30–32 mm ring vs reference 36–38 mm; scenario score 0.542 despite moderate complexity.
links.quote: In Scenario 14, which required selecting a mitral annuloplasty ring size from echocardiographic data, four of five models recommended 30–32 mm, whereas the reference answer indicated 36–38 mm.

links.outcome: Whether benchmark/exam performance predicts competence in complex clinical decision-making
links.effect: Top models scored well overall, but even O1 showed deficits in patient safety (0.600) and hallucination avoidance (0.667) on expert-designed scenarios.
links.quote: Our results highlight that strong performance by LLMs on standardized exams does not ensure safe or reliable application in complex, high-stakes clinical decision-making.

links.outcome: Inter-evaluator agreement (Fleiss' kappa) before and after viewing expert reference answers
links.effect: Kappa rose from 0.0834 (round 1) to 0.1298 (round 2) after reviewing reference answers.
links.quote: Agreement improved after the second-round review incorporating suggested answers ( κ = 0.1298; 95% CI: 0.0981–0.1615; p < 0.0001).

unlisted_practices: Two-phase blinded evaluation with reference answers to measure trust calibration (overacceptance/underrecognition)
Multi-agent prompting (seed responses synthesized by master prompt) for LLM output generation

links.effect: Fleiss' κ increased from 0.0834 to 0.1298 after suggested answers; both p < 0.0001.
links.quote: Agreement improved after the second-round review incorporating suggested answers ( κ = 0.1298; 95% CI: 0.0981–0.1615; p < 0.0001).

links.effect: Median normalized scores: O1 0.896, O3-mini-high 0.854, DeepSeek-R1 0.792, GPT-4 0.667, Llama3-OpenBioLLM-70B 0.521.
links.quote: Median normalized scores [25th–75th percentile] were highest for O1 [0.896 (0.667–0.990)], followed by O3-mini-high [0.854 (0.667–0.917)], DeepSeek-R1 [0.792 (0.510–1.000)], GPT-4 [0.667 (0.417–0.917)], and Llama3-OpenBioLLM-70B [0.521 (0.167–0.833)].

links.effect: Overacceptance was 7.57% versus underrecognition 2.59%, net trust calibration gap +4.98%; McNemar p < 0.001.
links.quote: The overall overacceptance rate (affirmative-to-negative revisions) was 7.57%, whereas the underrecognition rate (negative-to-affirmative revisions) was 2.59%, yielding a net trust calibration gap of +4.98% (McNemar's test, p < 0.001).

links.effect: Patient safety 0.507, hallucination avoidance 0.549, and clinical efficiency 0.597 were lowest across models.
links.quote: Across evaluation dimensions, scenario comprehension scored highest (0.920), while patient safety (0.507), hallucination avoidance (0.549), and clinical efficiency (0.597) were lowest across models.

links.outcome: expert clinician overacceptance of flawed LLM reasoning
